rationale: Two adjacent pie wedges are distinguishable only by color; their boundary contrast is 2.73:1, below 3:1. Color is required to identify which region each wedge represents.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: 'graphical objects ... required to understand the content' must have 3:1; F78 / G207 (use of a contrast of at least 3:1 with adjacent colors).

rationale: The data lines that carry the trend are 2.88:1 against the plot background, below 3:1. The line is required to understand the chart.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: graphical objects required to understand content need 3:1; G207; F78.

rationale: The boundary between the two stacked segments (the only cue for where fixed ends and variable begins) is ~1.2:1, far below 3:1.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11; F78 (failure due to insufficient contrast of graphical objects); G207.

rationale: The diagonal slash is the only part that conveys 'muted'; at ~2.5:1 it is below 3:1, so the icon's meaning is lost. The stroke is required to understand the icon.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: 'Graphics Required to Understand the Page'; G195/G207; F78.

rationale: Most segment boundaries pass, but one adjacent required pair is ~1.05:1. Under 1.4.11 the worst required part governs the component verdict.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11; F78; the 3:1 threshold applies to each graphical object 'required to understand'.

rationale: The two color-coded risk regions share a border at 1.45:1; color is required to read risk and the regions cannot be distinguished.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11; G207 (3:1 with adjacent colors); F78.

rationale: The connector/arrow that establishes the flow order is ~2.1:1 against the background, below 3:1; it is required to understand the diagram.
The needle is the part that communicates the gauge reading; at ~2.7:1 against the dial face it is below 3:1 and the value cannot be read.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: parts of graphics required to understand must be 3:1; G207; F78.

rationale: The triangle is a graphical object that conveys 'this field is required'; at ~2.35:1 it is below 3:1, so the required state is not perceivable.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11; the 'required to identify' scope; F78.

rationale: Group membership is encoded only by marker color; the two groups are ~1.2:1 to each other, so the required distinction is not perceivable.
All adjacent wedge pairs exceed 3:1, so each required boundary is perceivable.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: graphical objects required to understand meet 3:1; G207.

rationale: Both data lines exceed 3:1 against the plot background; required parts are perceivable.
The low-contrast wedge colors are redundant: an in-image text label identifies every wedge, so the color is not required to understand the chart and is exempt.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Understanding: 'if the information ... is also available in text' / G207 note that a part not required to understand is exempt.

rationale: The swoosh conveys no information and is not required to understand the logo; purely decorative graphics are exempt from 1.4.11.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: applies to graphics 'required to understand'; decorative graphics are out of scope.

rationale: The whole icon, including the meaning-bearing handle, is well above 3:1 against the background.
Bars (required to read the data) are far above 3:1 against the background.
The wedge sits over a varying photographic/gradient backdrop with no single adjacent color; a deterministic per-pixel verdict is not sound, so the runner must abstain rather than fail.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Understanding notes the comparison is against 'adjacent colours'; where the adjacent surface varies, deterministic single-value contrast is undefined.

rationale: A continuous gradient legend has no discrete adjacent boundaries to evaluate at 3:1; the runner cannot soundly assign a single ratio and must abstain.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: 3:1 is defined against discrete adjacent colors; continuous gradients are not deterministically evaluable.

rationale: The required connector/arrow is high contrast against the background.
The reading-bearing needle is well above 3:1 against the dial face.
The low-contrast element is a decorative drop shadow, not required to read the data; the actual data bars exceed 3:1.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: only parts 'required to understand' are in scope; decorative shadows are exempt.

rationale: The faint divider is an essential, verbatim reproduction documenting how the vendor UI actually looks; per the essential exception, altering it would change the information being conveyed.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Understanding: 'Essential: A particular presentation of the graphical object is essential to the information being conveyed.'
